body:
sq-7d3dj.16 removed the per-scan O(|added|) linear pass from `Overlay::count_correction` by caching a perm-sorted projection of `added` and binary-searching it. The `deleted` side of the SAME function is untouched and still iterates the whole `FxHashSet` on EVERY scan of a mutated store, so a delete-heavy overlay keeps the exact blow-up that bead just fixed for inserts.

Measured on the sq-7d3dj.16 work box (NON-CANONICAL, relative shape only), 1M-triple base, DELETE-only overlay, 10k bound-subject scans of ranges the overlay does not touch (all on the zero-copy fast path):

  d=16    2.1 ms
  d=1024  28.1 ms
  d=8192  239.3 ms

That is ~linear in |deleted| — the same curve the insert side showed before the fix (104 ms at k=8192, now flat at ~1.8 ms).

Not done in the sq-7d3dj.16 PR because the bead scopes itself to `added`, and `deleted` is a genuinely different change: it is an `FxHashSet` (chosen for the O(1) membership test `Overlay::merge` needs on the base-row loop), so it needs an ADDITIONAL sorted projection rather than a reinterpretation of an existing sorted Vec — i.e. the hash set has to stay, and the projections are new memory on top of it.

Suggested shape, mirroring what landed for `added`: a lazy per-perm `OnceLock<Vec<[Id;3]>>` sorted projection of `deleted`, invalidated in `apply_delta` alongside `invalidate_added`, used for the `del` count in `count_correction` (two binary searches). MEASURE-FIRST per the sq-7d3dj epic discipline — A/B the delete-only curve above before shipping.

> 🤖 Discovered by the SPARQ worker while implementing #3183. Out-of-scope for that PR; captured as follow-up.

The intended narrow change is a lazy sorted deletion projection for range counting, retaining the hash set used for membership. Validation will cover cache invalidation, mixed changes, snapshots/forks, cold and warm use, and the added memory cost, followed by actual independent Opus review before admission. The stopped indexed top-k experiment is tracked separately in #6465.

title: perf(store): cache perm-sorted overlay `deleted` projections too — count_correction is still O(|deleted|) per scan
